title: Grammar: Future Perfect, Future Continuous & Advanced Future Expressions
grammarTip:
Future Perfect и Future Perfect Continuous — для академического и профессионального уровня:

FUTURE PERFECT (will have + PP) → к определённому моменту в будущем:
"By June, I will have completed all the exams."
"By 2030, scientists will have found a solution."

FUTURE PERFECT CONTINUOUS (will have been + -ing) → сколько времени к моменту:
"By next year, I will have been studying English for five years."
"She will have been working here for ten years by March."

💡 Сигналы: by (next week / 2030 / the time...) · before · when
"When you arrive, I will have been waiting for an hour."

grammarTable.subject: Future perfect
grammarTable.example: "By 2030, the company will have invested $10bn in AI."

grammarTable.subject: Future perfect continuous
grammarTable.short: ongoing FROM past UNTIL future point
grammarTable.example: "By next year, she will have been working on this project for three years."

grammarTable.subject: Future continuous
grammarTable.short: action in progress AT a future time
grammarTable.example: "In 2040, millions will be using AI assistants daily."

grammarTable.subject: be about to
grammarTable.example: "Technology is about to reshape everything we know about work."

grammarTable.subject: be likely to / due to / expected to
grammarTable.example: "AI is likely to transform healthcare. The report is due to be published next year."

grammarTable.subject: shall (formal)
grammarTable.example: "We shall publish the findings by the end of the year." (formal written English)

rows.example: "By 2035, AI will have replaced most routine data entry jobs."

rows.form: By the time + clause: will have + pp
rows.example: "By the time the legislation passes, the technology will have moved on."
"The project will already have finished before the audit begins."

grammarExtra.title: Probability Expressions: Likely, Due, Expected, Predicted

rows.example: "AI is likely to augment rather than replace most jobs." (moderate probability)
"Global AI investment is expected to double by 2028." (based on evidence)
"The market is predicted to reach $500bn by 2030."
"The new regulations are due to come into effect in January."

rows.form: is/are about to + infinitive = very soon
rows.example: "The CEO is about to announce a major AI investment."
"She was just about to submit her report when the system crashed."

rows.form: Can also express something that nearly happened
rows.example: "We were about to launch when we discovered a critical bug."

grammarExtra.title: Future in Formal and Academic Writing

rows.form: Future perfect for milestones and deadlines
rows.example: "By Q3, the team will have completed the feasibility study."
"AI is expected to be regulated more strictly within the next five years."
"AI may well transform the economy, though the timeline remains uncertain."

grammarExtra.title: Common Errors with Advanced Future Forms

rows.form: ❌ By 2030, AI will replace all jobs.
rows.example: ✅ By 2030, AI will have replaced many routine jobs. (future perfect for by + time)

rows.form: ❌ She will have been working here since five years.
rows.example: ✅ She will have been working here for five years. (duration: "for" not "since")

rows.form: ❌ Technology is likely transforming the economy.
rows.example: ✅ Technology is likely to transform the economy. ("likely to + infinitive")

rows.form: ❌ The report is about publishing next month.
rows.example: ✅ The report is about to be published next month. ("about to + infinitive")

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct future perfect form.
exercises.text: "By 2035, researchers ___ a cure for most forms of cancer."
exercises.hint: "By + time" = future perfect: will have + pp

exercises.text: "By the time the regulation passes, the technology ___ (move) on significantly."
exercises.hint: "By the time" + future perfect: will have + pp

exercises.text: "Global AI investment ___ triple by 2030." (based on current forecasts)
"Next month, she ___ (work) on her AI dissertation for two years."
exercises.hint: Future perfect continuous: will have been + -ing (duration)

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct "be about to" form.
exercises.text: "The company ___ launch its AI assistant — the press conference is in five minutes."
exercises.hint: "is about to" = something happening very soon / immediately

exercises.instruction: Rewrite as a future perfect sentence.
exercises.correct: By 2040, AI will have transformed most white-collar jobs.
exercises.hint: "By + time" triggers future perfect: will have + pp

opts: AI is likely to transform healthcare.
exercises.correct: AI is likely to transform healthcare.

exercises.hint: "is due to + infinitive" = scheduled to happen at a specific time

exercises.text: "By next year, she will have been leading the AI team for a decade."
opts: She will start leading the team next year
She led the team ten years ago
By next year, her ten years of leadership will be complete
She is going to lead the team for one more year
exercises.correct: By next year, her ten years of leadership will be complete
exercises.hint: Future perfect continuous: the duration will be complete at the future point

exercises.instruction: Which sentence uses hedging language correctly?
opts: AI will certainly replace all doctors.
AI may well transform diagnostics, though the timeline is uncertain.
AI is about to completely changing medicine.
AI is going to will replace doctors.
exercises.correct: AI may well transform diagnostics, though the timeline is uncertain.
exercises.hint: "may well" = hedging probability; adds nuance to prediction

exercises.text: "By the time the course ends, students ___ (learn) three programming languages."
exercises.hint: "By the time" + future perfect: will have + pp

opts: The population is predicted grow to 10 billion by 2050.
The population is predicted to grow to 10 billion by 2050.
The population predicted to grow to 10 billion by 2050.
The population is predicted growing to 10 billion by 2050.
exercises.correct: The population is predicted to grow to 10 billion by 2050.

exercises.text: "The new AI regulations ___ (implement) across the EU next year."
exercises.correct: will be implemented / are expected to be implemented
exercises.hint: Formal passive future: will be + pp OR is expected to be + pp

exercises.text: "She will have been working here since three years by March."
exercises.hint: Duration (period of time): "for three years", not "since three years"

exercises.text: "In 2035, most people ___ (use) AI assistants as part of their daily routines."
exercises.hint: Future continuous: action in progress / typical activity at a future time

exercises.instruction: Choose the most sophisticated way to express this prediction formally.
exercises.text: "AI will probably be very important in healthcare by 2030."
opts: AI is going to be very important in healthcare by 2030.
AI will be very important in healthcare by 2030.
AI is predicted to play a significant role in healthcare by 2030.
AI is about to become important in healthcare by 2030.
exercises.correct: AI is predicted to play a significant role in healthcare by 2030.
exercises.hint: "is predicted to + infinitive" is the most formal and precise expression

questions.text: "By 2040, most routine jobs ___ by AI." Choose the correct form.
questions.hint: "By + time" = future perfect; passive = will have been + pp

questions.text: "The conference ___ (begin) — everyone is taking their seats." (happening right now / immediately)
questions.hint: "is about to + infinitive" = happening very soon

questions.text: "By next year, I ___ (study) programming for three years."
questions.hint: Future perfect continuous: will have been + -ing (duration until future point)

questions.text: "In 2050, people ___ AI tools as naturally as they use electricity today." (typical ongoing activity)
questions.hint: Future continuous: typical ongoing activity at a future time

questions.text: "Technology is likely to transform education" is grammatically correct.
"The new AI policy ___ (come) into effect in January." (scheduled event)
questions.hint: "is due to + infinitive" = scheduled/expected at a specific time

questions.text: "By the time the regulation passes, technology ___ already ___." Choose the correct option.
questions.hint: "By the time" + future perfect: will have + pp

questions.text: "AI ___ (likely / disrupt) the legal profession significantly over the next decade."
Which correctly uses hedging language for a prediction?
opts: AI will certainly replace all teachers.
AI may well transform aspects of education, though challenges remain.
AI is about to replace teachers soon.
AI is expected certainly to replace teachers.
questions.correct: AI may well transform aspects of education, though challenges remain.
questions.hint: "May well" = hedging — possible but not certain

questions.text: "She ___ (work) on AI research for over a decade by the time she receives her professorship."
questions.hint: Future perfect continuous: ongoing duration until a future point

questions.text: Which is the most formal way to express a prediction in academic writing?
opts: AI is going to change medicine.
I think AI will change medicine.
AI is predicted to transform medical diagnostics within the next decade.
AI is about to change medicine.
questions.correct: AI is predicted to transform medical diagnostics within the next decade.
questions.hint: "is predicted to + infinitive" = most formal, evidence-based, academic
